justification:
Verified with node tools/verify-page.mjs --drafts /databases/indexes/ (real run: lighthouse 97/100/100/100, consoleErrors=0, consoleWarnings=0, brokenLinks=0, mobileOverflowPx=0, 3542 words, 40 code blocks, 2 figures) plus a manual Puppeteer pass at the same mobile viewport with all three <details class="solution"> force-opened, since the standard verify-page screenshots never render solution content. All ~8 affected panels were read directly off real screenshots, not inferred from source: idx_visitor and idx_vd (mobile-dark parts 07-08, 10), idx_dv (part 11), idx_cover COVERING and idx_cover plain (part 13), all cross-checked once more in mobile-light (parts 07, 13, identical wrap points, theme makes no layout difference as round 1 already found), plus idx_sp (a), idx_sp (c) and idx_pci inside the two expanded solutions via the manual pass. Every one of the 8 clips at essentially the same point ('SEARCH hit USING IND' or 'SEARCH hit USING COV', 20-21 visible detail-column characters), and every one is immediately followed, in the very next paragraph of ordinary wrapped prose (not inside the code panel, so not subject to its clipping), by a sentence that quotes the complete literal detail string verbatim, e.g. 'detail now reads SEARCH hit USING INDEX idx_vd (visitor_id=? AND hit_at=?)', 'detail reads SEARCH hit USING INDEX idx_sp (status=? AND path=?), confirming (c)', 'detail now reads SEARCH hit USING INDEX idx_pci (path>? AND path<?)'. That sentence is never itself clipped in any screenshot checked (mobile-dark or mobile-light, folded or open state) because it is plain paragraph text at the content column's full width, not the horizontally-constrained code panel. So a phone reader who never resorts to pinch-zoom or horizontal scroll always has the complete SCAN-vs-SEARCH evidence somewhere on the page for all 8 panels, which resolves WRITER_GUIDE section 7's 'must not be the one that is cut off' bar even though the code panel itself, exactly as the writer found, still visually clips. This is a real, structural fix, not a cosmetic one, and it directly answers round 1's major finding.

Independently sanity-checked the writer's 'renaming can't fix it' claim rather than taking it on faith: the fixed id/parent/notused columns plus internal code-panel padding leave roughly 20-21 monospace characters of the detail column visible in every affected mobile screenshot (measured directly off pixel widths in the panel crops, not just asserted). 'SEARCH hit USING INDEX ' alone, before any index name appears, is 23 characters (S-E-A-R-C-H space h-i-t space U-S-I-N-G space I-N-D-E-X space); every clipped screenshot cuts mid-word inside 'INDEX' itself ('...USING IND'), which is exactly what a 20-21 character budget against a 23-character fixed prefix predicts. Shortening idx_visitor_date to idx_vd or idx_status_path to idx_sp cannot move that clip point, because the word that overflows the budget is part of SQLite's own fixed EQP vocabulary, not the index name; the index name and condition that follow are already off-screen before they start. This is a legitimate, verifiable finding, not the writer giving up early on an easy fix. The renames were kept anyway (harmless tidiness, and idx_vd/idx_dv makes the column-order contrast in that section easier to read at a glance) but they were never claimed as the fix, only the prose-quote pattern was, and that framing is accurate. On the layout question: a genuine structural fix exists in principle (shrink or truncate id/parent/notused, or drop them into a legend/caption instead of columns, or use a smaller monospace size and horizontal scroll indicator for just this table), but every one of those requires touching the site's shared code-block/table rendering (global.css and/or the markdown-to-table pipeline shared by every article on the site), which is explicitly out of scope for a single article's writer per CONTENT_PLAN's who-may-touch-what rules. Flagging it below as a minor for the integrator to consider as a future shell-level improvement, not as a writer failure this round.

issues.location: Shared code-block/EXPLAIN-QUERY-PLAN table rendering (referenced by every SQLite EQP example across the site, not this article alone); the layout constraint that makes id/parent/notused eat ~21 of ~40 visible mobile columns before detail starts.
issues.problem: The writer's finding that renaming indexes cannot fix the mobile clip point is correct and was independently verified (the fixed EQP vocabulary 'SEARCH hit USING INDEX ' alone is 23 characters against a ~20-21 character visible budget, so the clip lands inside SQLite's own fixed words, before any index name is reached). The prose-quote fallback this round is a genuine, working accessibility fix, but it treats the symptom per-panel rather than the shared cause. A real layout-level fix (shrinking or hiding the id/parent/notused columns on narrow viewports, or reflowing the four-column EQP table so 'detail' gets the width, or a smaller monospace size with a visible horizontal-scroll affordance) would fix every future article's EQP panels at once and let panels stand on their own without needing a hand-written prose echo every time.
